scams.name: The Matsuyama Kyabakura / Bottakuri Bar Overcharge
scams.description: You're walking through Matsuyama in Naha after dinner and a hustler in a suit pitches 'great bar upstairs, ¥3,000 set.' You take the elevator to the fourth floor, the room is dim, and the door clicks shut behind you. A bottle of 'champagne' arrives unrequested. Ninety minutes later the bill is ¥821,000 — the exact amount in a March 2021 documented case for seven bottles of champagne and six juices. July 2023 police raids on Matsuyama found 18 establishments paying yakuza protection money, and the entire district sits on the Okinawa Prefectural Police caution list.
scams.avoidance: Never take an elevator to an upstairs bar you were pulled into from the street in Matsuyama. Stay on Kokusai-dori — it is well-lit, ground-floor, and tourist-safe. If you're already inside and staff ask for your card before showing a printed menu with prices, stand up and leave; no order placed means no legal claim. If the door is blocked, dial 110 — Okinawa Prefectural Police run a dedicated bottakuri response unit for Matsuyama. Freeze the card from your issuer's app at the first sign of coercion.

scams.name: The Makishi Public Market Cooking-Fee Bait-and-Switch
scams.description: Fish vendors at Makishi Public Market quote unpriced seafood then charge ¥550-per-person cooking fees upstairs, including for non-eating family members. February 2026 review documented charging for 5 people when only 2 were eating. Prices change based on customer nationality with no posted rates.
scams.avoidance: Get fish prices in writing before purchase leaves counter. Confirm cooking-fee headcount in advance. Walk away from stalls refusing written pricing. Use Tomari Fish Market instead where prices are posted. Demand itemized receipt.
scams.location: Makishi Public Market, Kokusai-dori area, Naha

scams.name: The Naha Airport Shirotaku and Long-Distance Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: Illegal white-plate taxis (shirotaku) at airport arrivals refuse meters and charge 1.5× normal fares with no receipt. Even licensed Stand No.8 is rated 2.3 stars with drivers inflating fares via unnecessary expressway detours and forcing large taxis instead of medium vehicles.
scams.avoidance: Use Yui Rail monorail instead (¥270-330). Queue at Stand No.6 or No.7, not Stand No.8. Insist drivers use meters before departure. Book hotel transfers or use Go taxi app. Never follow unofficial curbside ride offers.
scams.location: Naha Airport arrivals and taxi stands

scams.name: The Rental Car "Neighbor Gas Station" Fuel Overcharge
scams.description: Rental car return counters direct customers to adjacent gas stations charging ¥197/L when market price is ¥165/L, creating ¥15-20/L premiums with no opportunity to comparison shop. Staff map specifically routes returns to overpriced partner stations.
scams.avoidance: Fill up at ENEOS or Cosmo stations 2+ km away. Check prices via GoGo.gs before returning. Photograph fuel gauge at pickup and return. Photograph all car panels at pickup for damage disputes. Decline optional insurance upsells.
scams.location: Naha Airport rental car return stations and nearby gas stations

scams.name: The Kokusai-dori Souvenir Fake-Discount and Hidden Table Charge
scams.description: A souvenir shop on Kokusai-dori displays a Shisa lion-dog figurine with '¥4,980' crossed out in red marker and '¥1,980 — today only' written above it. The ¥4,980 was never the real price; the same figurine is ¥1,680 at Ryubo Department Store four blocks away and ¥1,280 at Naha Airport. Down the street, a restaurant with English photos in the window seats you, brings an unrequested plate of tofu and vegetables, and later charges ¥550 per person for 'otoshi' that wasn't on the outside menu. A ¥2,000 lunch ends at ¥4,500 for two people.
scams.avoidance: Before buying any souvenir on Kokusai-dori over ¥1,000, check the same item on Amazon Japan or at Ryubo — if the Kokusai-dori price is more than 30% above Ryubo's, walk away. Naha Airport is usually cheaper still. For restaurants, ask 'otoshi wa arimasu ka?' (お通しはありますか？ — 'is there an otoshi charge?') before you sit down, and if the answer is yes, ask the price. Eating one block off Kokusai-dori, in the covered Heiwa-dori arcade or on Ukishima-dori, typically runs 30–40% less for the same dish.
scams.location: Kokusai-dori shopping street and side-street restaurants, Naha

scams.name: The US Military Card-Fraud and Juicy-Bar Targeting
scams.description: November 2024 Stars & Stripes reported 23 credit/debit card fraud cases at Kadena Air Base with charges appearing within 24 hours of Exchange/commissary purchases. Chatan and Kin-town juicy bars target service members with champagne pushes and drink-spiking, with specific establishments on III MEF off-limits lists.
scams.avoidance: Check MCIPAC-MCBB Bulletin 5800 off-limits list before visiting entertainment districts. Use credit over debit off-base. Set transaction alerts on all military banking. Pay cash at small bars. Leave immediately if drink tastes wrong and contact base clinic or call 110.
scams.location: Kadena Air Base, Camp Foster, Chatan and Kin-cho entertainment districts

scams.name: The Yonaguni and Rural Okinawa Ore-Ore Police-Impersonation Fraud
scams.description: Fake police officers call hotel rooms claiming accounts are used for fraud, directing transfers to fake safe accounts. A September 2024 tourist from Niigata lost ¥19 million; a Yonaguni visitor lost over ¥10 million. January-February 2026 saw 85 fraud cases with ¥400 million in losses.
scams.avoidance: Hang up immediately on cold police calls—Japanese police never call about accounts. Dial 110 independently to verify. Never transfer money to phone-identified accounts. Alert hotel staff of alarming calls. Never accept offers to visit ATMs from taxi drivers or strangers.
scams.location: Yonaguni Island, Yaeyama and Miyako islands, northern Okinawa Main Island
